newsitem.title: USA: Northeast Utilities warns N.Hampshire of lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Northeast Utilities warns N.Hampshire of lawsuit.

text.p: Northeast Utilities warned New Hampshire that its proposed plan to restructure and deregulate electricity rates would violate a contract agreement between the state and its subsidiary.

Northeast subsidiary Public Service Company of New Hampshire generates 1,200 megawatts on its system and buys another 207 megawatts from the state's independent producers under a court-ordered rate agreement. The company wrote a letter to New Hampshire Attorney General Jeffrey Howard pointing out what it sees as inequities under a new rate scheme.

If the new rate agreement goes into effect, Northeast lawyer Robert Knickerbocker, Jr warned Howard, "The state is at risk for the payment of hundreds of millions of dollars of damages to NU and PSNH..."

The proposed rate restructuring plan, PSNH said would result in stranded assets. The "actions would be a violation by the state of the Bankruptcy Court's order approving PSNH's restructuring plan..." Knickerbocker wrote.
Northeast Utilities purchased PSNH in 1988 after the utility went bankrupt.

The New Hampshire Legislature in 1995 ordered the Public Utilities Commission to develop a statewide electric utility plan aimed at reducing rates, increasing reliability and separate power generation from distribution and transmission.

The commission is reviewing a final plan which it hopes to issue on or before Feb. 28, 1997. It is this final plan which Northeast Utilities believes may violate the agreement it signed with the state when it took over PSNH in 1988.
